messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: panel size
parts:
Hi!

Is there an option to fix the size of a panel to some exact value? Since usually in plots the axis texts can have varying size, such that the resulting plot can have a panel which might change - even though I use the same width and height parameters for different plots (at least xyplot has this problem!). Is it assured in ggplot2 that the panel size is *always* the same if width and height are fixed or is there some other possibility to nail down the panel size. I definitely do not want changing panel sizes in a publication. In lattice I can set layout.width and layout.height to get the behavior I want, but I have not found an analogous option in ggplot.

Thanks a lot in advance. I really hope that there is a solution to this problem as these are (hopefully) the last problems from using ggplot "in production".

Sebastian

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: panel size
parts:
Hi,

I don't know if it can help, but the following hack is doing something
vaguely similar,

p1 <- qplot(1,1000, colour="test", linetype="longer legend") +
ylab("double\nline")
p2 <- qplot(1,1, colour="test") +
ylab("y")

source("http://ggextra.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/R/align.r")
align.plots(p1, p2)


The two plots have the same panel width, irrespective of the width of
the y label and legend. Maybe you could use a similar hack until
Hadley rewrites the layout.

HTH,

baptiste

don't use ggExtra unless you want to experiment, it's only a
collection of quick and dirty hacks.

I suggested this particular function not as a working solution but
maybe as an inspiration for a custom workaround. I admit it's very
ugly but that's all I can think of with the current ggplot2
implementation. The idea is to retrieve the size of the label and
legend of a plot, then push a grid viewport using these sizes. I think
it could be adapted to work for single plots, by setting the device
size.

Cheers,

baptiste

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: panel size
parts:
As an illustration of what I said earlier, the following creates two
separate plots that have the same width. You can also resize the
window in interactive use, the panel width remains constant. I added a
test with a grid.rect() of fixed width for comparison. I didn't
consider the plot margins, nor the height.

source("http://ggextra.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/inst/tests/fixedSize.r")

p1 <- qplot(1,1000, colour="test", linetype="longer legend") +
ylab("double\nline")
p2 <- qplot(1,1, colour="test") +
ylab("y")

test.rect <- function()
grid.rect(width=unit(5, "cm") - unit(3, "lines"),
gp=gpar(lty=2, col="red", fill="grey90"))

test <- opts(panel.background = test.rect)

g1 <- fixedsize(p1 + test, unit(5, "cm"))
g2 <- fixedsize(p2 + test, unit(5, "cm"))

pdf("test.pdf")
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(g1)
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(g2)
dev.off()


HTH,

baptiste
